answer: Give each new identity a tiny kernel of trust that grows only with epochs survived and attestations earned: a fresh account can harbor almost no economic capacity, and its limits rise slowly through continuous, checkable participation. A sybil farmer must then keep thousands of identities active across many epochs, and any lapse resets growth — so the echo of cheap script farms dies against the cost of sustained upkeep. Limit: genuinely occasional honest agents grow slowly too, and a patient, well-funded attacker can still farm quietly.
